reader.requirement: At --std 85, for each GIVING file-name-3 of a SORT: when that file contains variable length records, the SD's records must be refused if any is smaller than the smallest or larger than the largest record described for it; when it contains fixed length records, the SD's records must be refused if any is larger than its largest record. Whether a file without a RECORD clause, or with Format 3 (RECORD CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5), has fixed or variable records is implementor-defined (§1985:II.2.1.4.3, §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13).

reader.notes: One comparison of two RecordSizeRanges: the GIVING file bounds both ends when its records vary and only the top when they are fixed. That is the 1985 sentence. The implementor choices it leans on are documented (no RECORD clause: D-FRA; Format 3 variable: DOC-A.1-148). The one edition arm, the Format 3 bounds flag, gives the 1985 reading of 'records described'. Messages cite §2023:14.9.40.3 SR11.

refuter.evidence: §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR15 (under the FORMAT 3 heading, after GR13/GR14; the SD's RECORD clause is the same clause by §1985:XI.3.2.4 GR2) sizes each record of a format 3 file as 'the sum of the number of characters in all fixed length elementary items plus the sum of the maximum number of characters in any variable length item subordinate to the record'; GR14: 'the size of each data record is completely defined in the record description entry'. The 85 arm (VaryingRecordInfo.BoundsEnforced false) takes FileModel.VaryMin = Records.Min(MinRecordSize), which counts an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table at its MINIMUM occurrences (the Format 2 rule GR5a / §2023 GR8a), not GR15's maximum. Probes: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/sample-shared/out/refute-1985-08/r4-f3odo-clean.cob (GIVING G1 RECORD CONTAINS 8 TO 9 over G1R = 9 + X OCCURS 1 TO 7 DEPENDING (GR15 size 8) and G1S X(9); SD fixed 5): --std 85 RAN (admitted; 5 < smallest record 8 must be refused, DOC-A.1-148 makes format 3 variable); --std 2023 COBOL1757 '8 to 9 bytes but SW describes fixed-length records of 5'. E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/sample-shared/out/refute-1985-08/r4-sdf3odo-clean.cob (SD RECORD CONTAINS 6 TO 7 over SN 9 + X OCCURS 1 TO 5 DEPENDING (GR15 size 6) and X(7); GIVING VARYING 3 TO 8): --std 85 COBOL1757 'SW describes variable-length records of 2 to 7 bytes' (refuses legal source: SD records 6 and 7 lie in 3..8); --std 2023 RAN. Also E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/sample-shared/out/refute-1985-08/r4-f3odo.cob (RECORD CONTAINS 3 TO 8, one ODO record) RAN at 85. cite.py: 'OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR15 ... the text is in GR15'; 'OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR14 ... the text is in GR14'; 'OK §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR10 ... the text is in SR10'; 'OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13 ... the text is in GR13'.

refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING, cause (a): at --std 85 a format 3 file (GIVING or SD) whose record holds an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table is sized with the table at its minimum; GR15 sizes it at its maximum. Harm both ways: r4-f3odo-clean compiles (under-rejects) and r4-sdf3odo-clean is refused (rejects-legal-source). At --std 2023 both are judged by integer-4/integer-5 and come out right.

adjudication.reason: Mechanism 1 UPHELD, cause (a): at --std 85 a format 3 record holding an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table is sized at the table's minimum, where §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR15 sizes it at the maximum; harm both ways. The file names no verdict word for this mechanism: PARTIAL is the inventory's verdict for code that breaks part of the rule, the refuter's corrected verdict (NON-CONFORMING) in the vocabulary.
